title: Cardiac arrest: CPR and AED
summary: Unresponsive with absent or abnormal breathing: call, start CPR, and use an AED.
sources: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care — Adult Basic Life Support
actions: Make sure the scene is safe. Shout and tap the person’s shoulders to check responsiveness.
If unresponsive, send someone to call emergency services and get an AED. If alone, use the phone on speaker.
Check breathing for no more than 10 seconds. No breathing or only occasional gasps is not normal breathing.
Start chest compressions on the lower half of the breastbone at 100 to 120 per minute. For an adult, press at least 5 cm (2 in) but not more than 6 cm (2.4 in), allowing full recoil.

If trained and able, give 2 breaths after every 30 compressions. Each breath lasts about 1 second and should only make the chest rise. If unable to give breaths, continue compressions and follow the dispatcher.
Turn on the AED, attach pads as pictured, and follow its prompts. Nobody should touch the person during analysis or shock; restart CPR immediately afterward.
Continue until normal breathing returns, trained responders take over, or you are physically unable to continue.
prohibitions: Do not delay CPR to check a pulse if you are a lay rescuer.
Do not mistake occasional gasps for normal breathing.
Keep interruptions in compressions as short as possible.
tip: Rescue breaths are especially important after drowning, in children, and in opioid-associated emergencies.

emergencyCall.text: Cardiac arrest requires immediate emergency activation and CPR.
